summary_paragraph: A woman with a history of morbid obesity, COPD, chronic diastolic heart failure, obstructive sleep apnea, and tobacco use was admitted for hypoxia and altered mental status. She presented with respiratory failure likely due to a COPD exacerbation, volume overload from heart failure, and possible infection. She was intubated briefly due to increased work of breathing and required ICU care for oxygen support and monitoring. Treatment included IV diuretics, antibiotics initially for suspected pneumonia later narrowed to COPD exacerbation, and systemic steroids. A urinary tract infection was suspected due to positive initial culture but ruled out on repeat testing. She improved with treatment, regained mental clarity, and was transitioned to oral medications and nebulized bronchodilators. She was discharged to extended care with instructions to use oxygen, CPAP nightly, and nicotine patches to aid smoking cessation, with close monitoring for weight gain and respiratory symptoms.
